meta.label: Made by
meta.value: scripts/export_tracks.py in the simulation's repository, run by the GitHub workflow right after every engine run. It only reads the engine's saved state; it places, changes or cancels nothing.

meta.label: Input
meta.value: state/portfolio_state.json (the engine's saved state, read only), compared with out/portfolio.json and out/psummary.json of the same run

meta.label: How to read it
meta.value: One table with a section column: stats (one row of statistics and progress per track), equity (the strategy P&L curve by day), month, leg, symbol, signal (one row per closed signal), open (positions and queued orders now) and account (one row per firm programme). Track challenge is A, funded-start is B. Amounts are US dollars summed over a track's accounts, identical copies included.

meta.label: How the numbers are made
meta.value: * Strategy P&L of one account = everything its trades made or lost since the start, carried across phase resets and payouts: (trading result banked by every finished phase or attempt) + (rewards withdrawn) + (current equity - starting balance). A phase pass or a failed attempt puts the account's balance back to its starting size and a reward takes profit out of the account; neither is a trading loss or gain, so the curve does not jump there. A track's P&L is the sum over its accounts, each counted as many times as the firm allows identical copies. * One signal = the same entry (market, side, leg, entry date, entry price) taken by one or more accounts. Its result is the sum over those accounts; its R is that net result divided by the risk they took at entry. A signal counts as closed once no account still holds it. Win = net result above zero. * Drawdown is measured on the end-of-day strategy P&L curve of the track, from its highest point so far. * Everything that describes an account right now (room to the firm's loss limits, progress to the phase target, fees, rewards) is recomputed here with the engine's own formulas and compared with the engine's export of the same run (out/portfolio.json, out/psummary.json); any difference is reported in the selfCheck column.
